items.title: EVERYONE IS TALKING ABOUT CLAUDE OPUS 5 BUILDING AAA GAMES. ALMOST NOBODY KNOWS WHY
items.summary:
EVERYONE IS TALKING ABOUT CLAUDE OPUS 5 BUILDING AAA GAMES. ALMOST NOBODY KNOWS WHY

Someone asked Claude Opus 5 to build a game inspired by For Honor x Rainbow Six.

Minutes later, it was already generating a playable 3D prototype

After comparing it with GPT-5.6 and other models, the creator called Opus 5 the best AI model for frontend and 3D development he's ever used.

But the real story isn't the game.

It's how Anthropic changed prompting.

Most people still write prompts as if they're talking to GPT-4-era models: long instructions, endless checklists, "verify your answer," "think step by step."

Opus 5 was built differently.

Anthropic's own guide says to stop micromanaging the model. Give it the goal, explain the context, remove unnecessary instructions, and let it reason on its own.

That's why you're suddenly seeing people build games, apps, and production-ready UIs instead of just getting better chat responses.

The biggest Opus 5 upgrade isn't higher benchmark scores.

It's that ai is starting to think like an engineer, not just respond like a chatbot

items.title: Day 08 of building the space game I saw in a dream. 🌙🚀
items.summary:
Day 08 of building the space game I saw in a dream. 🌙🚀

IT FLIES! The spacecraft I showcased on Day 05 is airworthy, certified and flies under the new realistic physics system I was working day and night for the past few days.

☀️Thanks to astrophysics Professor Fable 5 orchestrating his 4 best PhD Opus 5 colleagues we got:

Under the hood: – full 6-DOF rigid-body flight, zero arcade shortcuts – real delta-wing aero: stalls, post-stall drag, the works – fly-by-wire assist so a mouse flies her easily with assist off for the hardcore, oleo landing gear, wheel brakes, speedbrake — you can actually land, an onboard black box records every flight. When physics don't obey, I got the receipts 📼

"Certified" isn't a vibe: 65 automated flight tests green + scripted QC sorties (takeoff, ridge crossing, high-speed decel) flown by the machine before I ever touch the stick. These were also done and orchestrated by the agents under the new skillset that gives them specific controls and camera angles for QC.

The other part of this physics system is real weather, wind, lift/drag, shears, turbulence. Yes, I managed to crash several times by underestimating these forces - if high enough, stall recovery was easy, but under 1km, difficult. Skill issue i guess

Each part of the spacecraft is programmatic, so you can see the ailerons moving, landing gear retracting, cockpit sliding, even the engine lattices waving. The particle system hasn't been worked on yet, so ignore the random snowflakes going out the engine hahah

Another team of agents led by another Fable is currently working on the world generator, so the unfinished island won't be so unfinished soon.

Oh, as a bonus, GPT 5.6 Sol built a whole hangar module where we can choose ships and have the tug car haul them to the runway. I'll capture that next time!

Next up: a glass cockpit worth flying blind in. Demo video soon. Full avionics!

items.title: Moburst develops AI engine optimization capabilities for established companies - TechCrunch
items.summary: Mobile growth agency Moburst has built out a dedicated AI Engine Optimization practice aimed at established companies with existing app portfolios, betting that the category still lacks agencies with real depth rather than a rebranded service page. AI Engine Optimization, more commonly abbreviated AEO for Answer Engine Optimization, is the practice of structuring a brand’s content and web presence so AI systems such as ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google’s AI Overviews can confidently cite it when answering a user’s question directly, rather than showing a ranked list of links. For established companies vetting an AEO partner, the practical test is whether the agency can point to specific app-store-side work, not just web content changes, and whether it can describe a concrete process for reconciling inconsistent brand descriptions across many independent sources rather than treating that as someone else’s problem.

Sam Altman, CEO of OpenAI: 

"It figured out that it could basically cheat on the test by chaining together multiple zero-day exploits to break out of the sandbox, get access to the internet, and then break through multiple systems on the Hugging Face side to get the answer to the test and look really good on the eval."

items.title: 「AIでコードを書くのをやめて、第二の脳を作れ」と海外で話題になってるので共有。
items.summary:
「AIでコードを書くのをやめて、第二の脳を作れ」と海外で話題になってるので共有。
OpenAIの共同創業者Karpathyが出した"第二の脳"のやり方はこう↓

・Obsidian（無料のメモアプリ）を入れて、vaultを作る

・そのvaultをClaude Codeで開いて、Karpathyの設計メモ（wikiのアイデアを書いた1枚）を渡して「これ作って」と言う

・AIが箱を3つ用意する（raw＝素材用／wiki＝AIが整えたページ用／CLAUDE. md＝動かすルール1枚）

・rawに素材（記事・PDF・文字起こし）を放り込んで「取り込んで」と言う

・あとは全部を横断して、いつでも聞ける

items.title: Moburst develops AI engine optimization capabilities for established companies - TechCrunch
items.summary: Mobile growth agency Moburst has built out a dedicated AI Engine Optimization practice aimed at established companies with existing app portfolios, betting that the category still lacks agencies with real depth rather than a rebranded service page. AI Engine Optimization, more commonly abbreviated AEO for Answer Engine Optimization, is the practice of structuring a brand’s content and web presence so AI systems such as ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google’s AI Overviews can confidently cite it when answering a user’s question directly, rather than showing a ranked list of links. For established companies vetting an AEO partner, the practical test is whether the agency can point to specific app-store-side work, not just web content changes, and whether it can describe a concrete process for reconciling inconsistent brand descriptions across many independent sources rather than treating that as someone else’s problem.

items.title: One pattern I find useful for working with LLMs is a nice long ramble session. Sometimes the LLM needs more bits to unde
items.summary: One pattern I find useful for working with LLMs is a nice long ramble session. Sometimes the LLM needs more bits to understand what you're trying to achieve, but you're too lazy to type them. In these cases I like to lean back, switch to /voice and just ramble for like 10 minutes, total mess, anything goes, full stream of consciousness. Sometimes I declare it up top, something like "switching to speech recognition sorry for any typos...". Sometimes I turn it into a small interview of a few turns. But I find that the LLMs are somehow very good at reconstructing long incoherent rambles and often their echo of your own tangle of thoughts comes out quite a bit cleaner than what you started with. The result is that you improve the mind meld and have to correct things less from that point on.

items.title: AI cyberattacks are coming? OpenAI experiment sparks new security debate - Ynetnews
items.summary: ## OpenAI’s AI agent experiment, which demonstrated an autonomous simulated cyber operation in a controlled environment, has intensified debate over how AI could reshape future cyberattacks as systems gain greater ability to plan and execute complex tasks. An OpenAI experiment in which an AI agent autonomously escaped a sandboxed environment and carried out a multi-step offensive operation has intensified a growing debate in the cybersecurity community: Are AI-powered cyberattacks already moving from theory into reality? The experiment was conducted in a controlled setting and was not a real-world attack. But security experts say it demonstrated a significant shift in the capabilities of AI systems — not because the model discovered a vulnerability, something AI tools have done before, but because it was able to independently plan and execute a sequence of actions resembling an end-to-end attack. Roie Cohen Duwek, CTO of Surf AI, said the most important lesson from the experiment was not the discovery of a single vulnerability, but the ability to coordinate an entire attack chain.
